approach: Add the reclaim in disk.rs: `sweep_interrupted_targets` plus `Athena::reclaim_interrupted`. They remove only `target/` of jobs that are Dispatched in Records, have no live registry entry, are not in a keep list, and whose job lock can be taken (held during removal). In drain.rs add a defaulted `Steps::reclaim_interrupted(own: &[String])`, called once at drain start (before `steps.queue()`) and in `run_job` before `steps.run`, with the drain's own jobs (this item plus every item in `tried`) as the keep list. `RealSteps` forwards to the Athena method. The new tests in drain.rs drive `drain` through `RealSteps` over a real fixture. The fixture is shared with the integration tests by `#[path = "../tests/common/mod.rs"] mod common;` inside the drain.rs test module, so no other file changes. Finding 1 gets its test: low free space, no producer invocation, held as `environment: low disk`, no attempt used. The plan says plainly that this exercises the existing dispatch gate (run/mod.rs:749), because the producer starts at run/producer.rs, outside the three listed files, and `StageSink::enter` returns `()`. Whether to add producer.rs for a gate nearer the producer is routed to the user, and criterion 2 is not marked met until they answer.

decisions.choice: Criterion 2 gets a real test through `drain` with `RealSteps`, plus a scope question to the user; no duplicate drain-level gate.
decisions.reason: Finding 1: a test of the observable fits in drain.rs. With `StateDir::with_free_space` set low, a driver script that counts Producer invocations sees none, the item ends `environment: low disk`, the job stays Proposed with no outcome (no attempt used) and the hold text matches LOW_DISK. It is run through `go` for real, so it fails if the dispatch gate (run/mod.rs:749) is removed. The code shows the producer is entered at run/producer.rs:153 and `StageSink::enter` returns `()`, so a gate at the producer's own start needs producer.rs. That is a scope decision for the user. The plan states it and does not call the dispatch check a new check.

rejected.why: Same threshold, same job, a few lines before `go` repeats it at 749; a double that skips `go` would pass it falsely.
`enter` returns `()`, so it cannot hold a job.
Criterion 6 and the brief's file list allow three files only; left as open question 1.

decisions.choice: Reclaim `target/` only, through `StateDir::remove_target`, for jobs Dispatched in Records, with no registry entry after `registry().reap()`, not in the keep list, and whose `try_lock_job` succeeds (lock held while removing). Check the cheap predicates first, then the lock, so closed jobs get no new lock file.
decisions.reason: The brief keeps work tree and candidate. `status.rs:1615-1616` already calls Dispatched-and-not-running 'interrupted'. `go_job` takes the job lock at run/mod.rs:308 before the Dispatched record is committed, and registry entries appear only when a process group starts, so the lock covers the window the registry misses.

rejected.why: It is filtered to drained channels and drops jobs a retry already names, so some interrupted directories would stay.
Deletes the work tree; out of scope.
Gap between the Dispatched commit and the first process spawn.
That rule runs only once disk is already low; the fault is that nothing runs it earlier.

decisions.choice: Finding 2: the keep list is the drain's own jobs. `reclaim_interrupted(own: &[String])` is called with `[]` at drain start and with the item's job plus every id in `d.st().tried` in `run_job`. The sweep never touches those jobs and so never takes their lock.
decisions.reason: `go_job` uses `try_lock_job` and bails with 'already running' (run/mod.rs:308-310); a sweep holding a drain job's lock while it removes a large `target/` could make a worker's `go` fail falsely. The `tried` set is every item handed to a worker (drain_with: `d.st().tried.extend(wave)`). The drain reads an interrupted item again as a retry (a new job id), so it never calls `go` on the interrupted id itself. A new job is Proposed, not Dispatched, until dispatch, and holds its lock from `go_job` on, so the sweep skips it on either test. The race that remains is an outside `athena retry X` or `athena go X` on an interrupted X in the instant the sweep holds X's lock; it shows as an 'already running' error to that person and is named as a risk.

rejected.why: Does not protect the jobs of other workers in a concurrent drain.

rejected.option: Probe the lock without holding it (`lock_held`)
rejected.why: The remove could then overlap a job that has just started building; a rebuilt cache is cheaper than a failed build, but this still races. Keeping the lock and the keep list is safer.

decisions.choice: Tests use the real production rule, not a closure. disk.rs: `code_health::tests::set_up()` plus an `AnyRecord::Job` stub committed with `commit_records`. drain.rs: `RealSteps` over `common::Fixture`, which uses `make_athena` with a `Script`.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: `make_athena(git: &Git, state_root: &Path, capabilities: Vec<Box<dyn Capability>>, script: Script) -> Athena` (test_support.rs:748) sets `plenty_of_space` and a `FakeAgentDriver` with the state registry. `common::Fixture::athena(script)` in tests/common/mod.rs:173 builds an `Athena` the same way, and `Scenario::default().script()` is the `Script` the integration tests pass. common/mod.rs imports only athena_core, athena_agent, athena_data, athena_git, serde_json and tempfile (never athena_cli) and has `#![allow(dead_code)]`, so `#[path]` inclusion in the drain.rs test module compiles.

rejected.why: Never runs the Records, registry or lock rule.

rejected.option: New fixtures built from scratch in drain.rs
rejected.why: Too large; `#[path]` reuse needs no other file.

decisions.choice: Inject free space with `athena.state = athena.state.clone().with_free_space(fn)`, as tests/drain.rs:1498 does, not the process-wide `ATHENA_FREE_BYTES`.
decisions.reason: It is the same `FreeSpace` seam that `df_free_bytes` and its env hook feed; unit tests share one process, so an env var would leak between parallel tests.

disk.rs: add `pub fn sweep_interrupted_targets(state: &StateDir, interrupted: &dyn Fn(&JobId) -> bool, keep: &[JobId], ui: &dyn Ui) -> u64`. It iterates `state.job_ids()`, skips `keep`, tests `interrupted` first, then `try_lock_job` (skip if None), then calls the helper. Add `impl Athena { pub fn reclaim_interrupted(&self, keep: &[JobId], ui: &dyn Ui) -> u64 }`: `self.state.registry().reap()`, `Records::load(&self.git, &self.head()?)` once, and a job is interrupted when `state() == JobState::Dispatched` and `!self.running(id)`. A failed head or load prints a `warning:` line and returns 0.

risks.risk: The sweep removes a live job's build directory, or holds a lock a starting job needs.
risks.mitigation: It requires Dispatched in Records, no registry entry after `reap()`, a lock that `try_lock_job` can take, and a job outside the keep list. The lock covers the window before any process is registered. Test 3(a) covers lock, registry, closed and keep cases; test 3(b) covers a lock held during a drain.

risks.risk: Race with an outside `athena retry X` or `athena go X` on an interrupted X while the sweep holds X's lock: that command fails with 'already running in another athena process'.
risks.mitigation: The drain's own jobs are never swept, so its workers cannot hit this. The lock is held only while one `target/` is removed. The error names the cause and a rerun succeeds. Named in the CHANGELOG and docs.

risks.risk: Reading criterion 2 as met by the reclaim, or by the dispatch gate test.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG, module docs and open question 1 say that the dispatch check is the only disk check before the producer. Criterion 2 stays open until the user answers.

risks.risk: A resumed interrupted job loses a build cache it could reuse.
risks.mitigation: Only `target/` is removed; the criterion 1 test asserts the work tree and resume mark remain.

risks.risk: A Records read at drain start and per job stalls or aborts the drain.
risks.mitigation: One load per sweep; an unreadable head or records prints a `warning:` line and returns 0 bytes. It never fails the drain.

risks.risk: A new trait method breaks existing `Steps` implementors; clippy -D warnings trips on the `#[path]` include or new code.
risks.mitigation: A default no-op body keeps implementors compiling; step 9 runs the whole workspace checks.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in `mod tests` of drain.rs, entering through `drain(&RealSteps, limits, &Quiet)`. Include the shared fixture with `#[path = "../tests/common/mod.rs"] mod common;`. Build `common::Fixture::new()` and `fx.athena(Scenario::default().script())`. Make a job interrupted as `interrupt()` does at tests/drain.rs:3406: `ask`, then `go` with a producer killed by the script (`killing_producer` pattern), then `git reset --hard HEAD~1` until `Records` says Dispatched with no outcome, on a non-drained channel (`request_on(&athena, "web", ..)`), so the drain neither retries nor works it. Plant `jobs/<id>/target/debug/big` (100 KB), `jobs/<id>/work/main.rs`, and a resume mark with `StateDir::write_resume`. Run `drain` with the real steps and a `Lines` ui. No process is registered and no lock is held.
demonstrations.observes: After `drain` returns, `jobs/<id>/target` is gone. `work/main.rs` has its original bytes and the resume mark still reads back. The ui shows `disk       removed build directory of job <id>` with no job having been run (the queue held no work), so the removal came from the drain-start call.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `steps.reclaim_interrupted(&[])` call in `drain_with`, `target/` is still there and the test fails. A whole-directory removal fails the work-file and resume-mark asserts. A wrong Records filter (closed jobs only) leaves the Dispatched job's directory.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `drain::drain` with `RealSteps` (exists, drain.rs:2759). Fixture `common::Fixture` and `Scenario` via the `#[path]` include (exist, tests/common/mod.rs). `Steps::reclaim_interrupted` and `Athena::reclaim_interrupted` are added by plan steps 1 to 4; the double is the real `RealSteps`, and the rule under test (Records, registry, lock) is production code.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in drain.rs `mod tests`, through `drain` with `RealSteps`. Config `with_min_free_gb(&test_config(), 10)` (needs 10 GB). Wrap `Scenario::default().script()` in a `Script` that increments an `Arc<AtomicUsize>` for `spec.role == Role::Producer`. Set `athena.state = athena.state.clone().with_free_space(low)` where `low` returns 3_000_000_000 bytes. Queue one request with the `queue_steward_request` helper pattern (tests/drain.rs:1369, ported into the module). Run `drain`.
demonstrations.observes: The item's outcome is `environment: low disk`; the text carries `3.0 GB` and `10.0 GB`; no failure, no landing; the producer counter is 0; `Records` shows the job Proposed with no job record and no outcome (no attempt used); `disk::read_hold` gives the amounts. This holds at the dispatch gate (run/mod.rs:749). Whether a second gate at the producer's own start is wanted (open question 1) is for the user to answer; criterion 2 is not marked met for that.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the dispatch gate were removed, the producer counter would be 1 and the outcome would not be `environment: low disk`. The test also fails if the hold were counted as a failure or an attempt.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `drain::drain` with `RealSteps` (exists), `StateDir::with_free_space` set on the public `Athena.state` (exists, used at tests/drain.rs:1498), fake driver counting calls through the script (exists as the pattern at tests/drain.rs:1491). Plan step 7 adds the test.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. (a) disk.rs unit `the_interrupted_sweep_keeps_live_jobs_and_reclaims_dead_ones`, on `code_health::tests::set_up()`: commit four Job stubs (JSON as `dispatched_job_stub` at reading.rs:5799, with a distinct id each) with `commit_records(&[NewFile::record(&AnyRecord::Job(..))], ..)`; close one with `code_health::tests::close_job`. Give each job dir `target/` and `work/`. Job A has no process. Job B has a live `sleep 60` child (`process_group(0)`, `registry().register(pgid, id, ..)`, a `Reaper` guard that kills and waits). Job C's lock is held by `try_lock_job`. Job D is the closed one. Call `athena.reclaim_interrupted(&[], &ui)`, then with E in the keep list. (b) drain.rs unit `a_sweep_before_the_second_producer_reclaims_a_newly_interrupted_job`: real steps, two queued requests, `limits` set to work both. A live-looking Dispatched job on another channel has its lock held by the test via `try_lock_job`. The script hook, on the first Producer call, makes a second interrupted job's `target/` appear (a crash while that run goes). On the second Producer call it records whether that directory and the live job's exist.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core the_interrupted_sweep_keeps_live_jobs_and_reclaims_dead_ones && cargo test -p athena-cli a_sweep_before_the_second_producer_reclaims_a_newly_interrupted_job
demonstrations.observes: (a) Only A's `target/` is removed; B (registry), C (lock), D (closed) and the keep-listed job keep theirs; every `work/` stays. (b) When the second producer starts, the newly interrupted job's `target/` is gone and the live job's remains; the first job's own directory was never touched.
demonstrations.fails_without: A sweep ignoring the registry removes B's; ignoring the lock removes C's; filtering on closed instead of Dispatched removes D's and leaves A's. A drain that sweeps only at start leaves the new directory in place when the second producer starts, failing (b). Dropping the `run_job` call does the same.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::reclaim_interrupted` (added by step 2) and `drain::drain` with `RealSteps` (exists). Fixtures `set_up`, `close_job`, `Registry::register`, `try_lock_job`, `common::Fixture` all exist. The rule under test is production code; the only injected thing is the script hook that creates a directory, which stands for the crash.

open_questions: Scope decision for the user: criterion 2 asks for a disk check at the producer. The producer starts in run/producer.rs `producer_loop` (line 153 enters the stage, then `invoke_and_record`), outside the three listed files, and `StageSink::enter` returns `()`. The only check before it is the dispatch gate at run/mod.rs:749 (and the check before the checks at 1301). Add run/producer.rs (a `disk_gate` call before `invoke_and_record`, holding the job as `hold_for_disk` does and also covering send-back reruns), or accept the dispatch gate as the pre-producer check? Until answered, the test for criterion 2 exercises the dispatch gate and the criterion is not marked met.
